# Generated files and symbols

> The files beak prepare writes, which are committed, when each is rewritten, and every symbol generated for a schema class.

`beak prepare` reads your schema classes, resource classes, screens and `beak.yaml` and writes the wiring around them. This page lists every file it writes, whether you commit it, when it is rewritten, and each symbol generated for a schema class. Nothing here is hand-edited: a change belongs in the schema class or in `beak.yaml`, followed by `beak prepare`.

## Import

The generated symbols of a schema live in a `part` of the schema's own library, so you import the schema file and get them with it.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.dart"
import 'package:beak/beak.dart';
import 'package:beak/schema.dart';

part 'note.beak.dart';
```

The wiring files under `lib/beak/` are libraries of their own:

```dart
import 'beak/app.g.dart';       // BeakApp, beakPanelConfig
import 'beak/server.g.dart';    // beakHost()
import 'beak/registry.g.dart';  // beakModels, buildBeakRegistry()
```

## Summary

| Path | Committed | Rewritten | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<schema>.beak.dart`, next to each schema class | yes | when the schema changes | Columns, relations, fields, model, draft and record view of one schema |
| `lib/beak/registry.g.dart` | yes | when a model is added or removed | `beakModels`, `buildBeakRegistry()` |
| `lib/beak/panel.g.dart` | yes | when models, resource classes, screens or `beak.yaml` change; only with a generated entrypoint | `buildBeakPanel()` |
| `lib/beak/app.g.dart` | yes | when `beak.yaml` changes; only with a generated entrypoint | `beakPanelConfig`, the `BeakApp` widget |
| `lib/beak/server.g.dart` | yes | when migrations, seeders, models or `beak.yaml` change | `beakHost()` |
| `lib/main.dart` | no, git-ignored | as above, until you own it | `void main() => runApp(const BeakApp())` |
| `bin/serve.dart` | no, git-ignored | as above | Serves the API until `SIGINT` or `SIGTERM`; a refused setting, a taken port included, ends it with one line and exit `78` |
| `bin/migrate.dart` | no, git-ignored | as above | Runs migrations and seeders (`migrate`, `db:seed`, `migrate:fresh`) through `beakHost().runCli(args)`; a refused setting ends with one line and exit `78` |
| `lib/migrations/create_<table>_table.dart` | yes | never: written once, then yours | The migration for a table without one |

The `lib/beak/*.g.dart` files are committed so a fresh clone analyzes before any `beak` command runs. The three entrypoints sit at the paths Flutter and Dart expect and change nothing worth reviewing, so the scaffold's `.gitignore` excludes them.

`beak prepare` also refreshes the files coding agents read (the managed block in `AGENTS.md` and the docs of the resolved Beak version), as the `agents:` section of `beak.yaml` allows. See [CLI commands](cli-commands.md).

A package that holds schema classes only (it depends on `beak_core` and not on the app) gets the `.beak.dart` parts and `lib/beak/registry.g.dart` and nothing else: no panel, server, entrypoint or migration.

## Headers and staleness

Every wiring file of an app starts with the same two lines:

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/beak/registry.g.dart"
// GENERATED BY `beak prepare` — DO NOT EDIT.
// Run `beak prepare` after changing a schema class, a resource class, a screen or beak.yaml.
library;
```

The registry of a schema-only package has a shorter second line, `// Run `beak prepare` after changing a schema class.`, because it has no resource, screen or `beak.yaml` to change. A schema part carries `// Regenerated from the @Resource class in this library.` as its second line. The rules:

- `beak prepare` writes a file only when its contents change, which keeps Flutter's file watcher quiet under `beak dev`.
- An entrypoint (`lib/main.dart`, `bin/serve.dart`, `bin/migrate.dart`) whose first line is not `// GENERATED BY` belongs to you and is left alone. `beak eject main` writes such a `lib/main.dart`, see [CLI commands](cli-commands.md).
- When `beak.yaml` sets `panel.entrypoint`, `beak prepare` neither writes nor compares `lib/main.dart`.
- With `panel.entrypoint` or an authored `lib/main.dart`, nothing imports `lib/beak/panel.g.dart` and `app.g.dart`, so `beak prepare` neither writes nor compares them, and deletes a pair a generated entrypoint left behind. A project file that imports either one keeps both.
- Generation stops at the first batch of errors: no wiring is written, every problem is listed and the exit code is `1`. Schema parts are written ahead of the scan, so a refused run can have refreshed some, and says which.
- `beak doctor` byte-compares every generated file with what `beak prepare` would write.

Real output from a project with two models, `Note` and `Tag`, related through `@BelongsToMany`:

```console
$ beak prepare
  2 models · 0 resource classes · 0 screens · 0 overrides
  generated  7 of 11 files
  agents     up to date · docs not materialized: .dart_tool/package_config.json not found; run `flutter pub get` first
```

The count is files written out of the files `beak prepare` considered in this project, the schema parts included whether they changed or not. Two of the seven are migrations for the new `tags` table and the `note_tag` pivot. After a schema edit with no `beak prepare`:

```console
$ beak doctor
  FAIL generated files out of date (0 missing, 1 stale)
       → beak prepare
       → beak migrate
```

And after an unsupported field type:

```console
$ beak prepare
Cannot generate: fix these first:
  lib/resources/notes/models/tag.dart: Tag.tint is a Uri, which Beak cannot map to a column. Use a supported type, annotate it with @BelongsTo / @HasMany for a relationship, or @Custom for an opaque value.
```

## What beak prepare reads

| Source | Found by | Becomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Resource` classes | Any `.dart` file under `lib/`, except `*.beak.dart`, `*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart` and names starting with `_` | A part file, and an entry in the registry |
| Hand-written `BeakModel` subclasses | A class that extends `BeakModel` (directly, or through one class in the scanned set) with a zero-argument `const` constructor | An entry in the registry |
| `BeakResource` subclasses | Under `lib/`, matched to a model by the table its model reports | Replaces that model's default resource in `panel.g.dart` |
| Screens | Top-level `BeakScreen` declarations in `lib/screens/` | The panel's `pages:` |
| Migrations | `Migration` subclasses in `lib/migrations/` | `server.g.dart`, ordered by their declared `name` |
| Seeders | `Seeder` subclasses in `lib/seeders/` | `server.g.dart` |
| `beak.yaml` | Project root | Title, API URL, sidebar, icons, groups, hidden resources, `panel.entrypoint` |
| Override files | `lib/panel.dart`, `lib/theme.dart`, `lib/auth.dart`, `lib/server.dart` | See below |

```dart
/// The convention files a project may supply to override a Beak default.
///
/// Each is optional: absent means Beak uses its own default, and nothing
/// about it appears in the project.
enum BeakOverrideKind {
  /// `lib/panel.dart` — the whole panel config, last word.
  panel(path: 'panel.dart', symbol: 'beakPanel'),

  /// `lib/theme.dart` — light and dark themes.
  theme(path: 'theme.dart', symbol: 'beakLightTheme'),

  /// `lib/auth.dart` — auth routes and callbacks.
  auth(path: 'auth.dart', symbol: 'beakAuth'),

  /// `lib/server.dart` — middleware, extra routes and policy.
  server(path: 'server.dart', symbol: 'beakServer');

  const BeakOverrideKind({required this.path, required this.symbol});
```

An override applies only when its file declares the named top-level function. `beakPanel(BeakPanelConfig)` has the last word on the panel config. `beakLightTheme` and `beakDarkTheme` set the themes, `beakAuth` the auth config, and `beakServer` configures the host. A `beakStorageRegistry` function in `lib/server.dart` registers storage drivers without replacing the default server.

A hidden resource (`beak.yaml`) keeps its model and its API and drops out of `panel.g.dart`.

## The schema part

`beak prepare` writes six things into each part, in this order:

```dart
_writeColumns(buffer, schema);
_writeRelations(buffer, schema, byClass, all);
_writeFields(buffer, schema, byClass);
_writeModel(buffer, schema, all);
_writeDraft(buffer, schema, byClass);
_writeRecord(buffer, schema, byClass);
// Formatted here rather than by the caller, so any consumer of the
// emitter gets source that `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` accepts.
return BeakEmitters.format(buffer.toString());
```

For a schema `X`:

| Symbol | Kind | Emitted | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `XColumns` | `abstract final class` | always | One `static const` column per field, plus implied columns, and `values` |
| `XRelations` | `abstract final class` | when `X` has a relationship or is the target of an inverse | One `static const` relationship per relationship, including generated inverses |
| `XFields` | `final class` | always | Typed field references, one getter per column and relationship |
| `XToOneField` | `final class` | always | The same references reached through a to-one path |
| `XModel` | `final class extends BeakModel` | always | The model: static references, `options`, `search`, metadata overrides |
| `_XModelFormSlot` | private `enum` | always | Field slots the auto forms claim |
| `XDraft` | `final class` | always | Nullable live view of an unsaved form draft |
| `XDraftAccess` | `extension` on `BeakDraftReader` | always | `draft.asX` |
| `XRecord` | `extension type` over `BeakRecord` | always | Typed reads of a fetched record |
| `XRecordAccess` | `extension` on `BeakRecord` | always | `record.asX` |

### XColumns

The columns in declaration order, preceded by the implied ones (see [Annotations](annotations.md#columns-the-resource-adds)). Each is a `static const` of the column class its Dart type selects, named after the field, with the schema's doc comment. Non-nullable fields get `BeakRequired()` first in `rules`, and a `BeakMaxLength` or `BeakMin`/`BeakMax` rule also fills `maxLength` or `min`/`max`.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.beak.dart"
abstract final class NoteColumns {
  /// Primary key.
  static const BeakStringColumn id = BeakStringColumn(
    key: 'id',
    label: 'Id',
    visibleOn: {BeakContext.detail},
  );

  /// What the note is called.
  ///
  /// Non-nullable, so it is required: the form validator, the API and the
  /// schema all derive that from the type rather than restating it.
  static const BeakStringColumn title = BeakStringColumn(
    key: 'title',
    label: 'Title',
    rules: [BeakRequired(), BeakMaxLength(255)],
    searchable: true,
    sortable: true,
    maxLength: 255,
  );
  // ...
  /// Every column, in declaration order.
  static const List<BeakColumn> values = [
    id,
    title,
    // ...
  ];
}
```

### XRelations

One `static const` per relationship, named after the field, of the `BeakBelongsTo`, `BeakHasOne`, `BeakHasMany` or `BeakBelongsToMany` class. It carries the related table, the related display column, the foreign key or pivot names, and the picker's `searchColumnKeys`. The other side is generated too: a `@BelongsTo` on `Book` adds `AuthorRelations.books`, a has-many named after the plural table. A `@HasMany` or `@HasOne` adds a belongs-to named after the singular table, and a `@BelongsToMany` is mirrored. The inverse is skipped when the far class already declares any relationship to the owner, or when the annotation says `inverse: false`.

```dart title="packages/beak_core/lib/src/relations/beak_has_many.dart"
const BeakHasMany({
  required super.key,
  required super.label,
  required super.relatedTable,
  required super.displayColumnKey,
  required this.foreignKey,
  super.searchColumnKeys,
  this.onDelete = BeakOnDelete.restrict,
  this.owned = false,
});
```

### XFields and XToOneField

`XFields` is the typed reference set every configuration is written with. Each column is a `BeakScalarField<T>`, where `T` is the field's Dart value type (`String`, `int`, `double`, `bool`, `DateTime`, the enum, `BeakDate`, `BeakDecimal`, and so on). Each to-one relationship is an `XToOneField`, and each to-many relationship a `BeakToManyField`. The `.via(model, path)` constructor roots the same set at another model, so `OrderItemModel.variant.price` reads the price of the related variant.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.beak.dart"
final class NoteFields {
  /// Creates the fields of Note, rooted at its own model.
  const NoteFields() : _model = const NoteModel(), _path = const [];

  /// Creates fields rooted at [model] and reached through [path].
  const NoteFields.via(this._model, this._path);
  final BeakModel _model;
  final List<BeakRelationship> _path;

  /// Id.
  BeakScalarField<String> get id => BeakScalarField<String>(
    model: _model,
    column: NoteColumns.id,
    path: _path,
    isRequired: false,
  );
  // ...
}
```

### XModel

A `final class` that extends `BeakModel`. Beyond the overrides below, every field and relationship gets a `static final` shortcut (`NoteModel.title`) that points at `NoteModel.fields.title`.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.beak.dart"
final class NoteModel extends BeakModel {
  /// Creates the notes model.
  const NoteModel();

  /// Typed field and relation references, including reserved names.
  static const NoteFields fields = NoteFields();
  // ...
  /// Declarative source for record choices.
  static BeakOptionQuery options({BeakFilter? filter}) => BeakOptionQuery(
    model: const NoteModel(),
    query: const NoteModel().query(filter: filter),
  );

  /// Searches the model display and searchable columns.
  static BeakOptionQuery search(String term, {BeakFilter? filter}) =>
      BeakOptionQuery(
        model: const NoteModel(),
        query: const NoteModel().query(
          filter: filter,
          search: BeakSearch(term, const ['title']),
        ),
      );

  @override
  String get table => 'notes';

  @override
  String get displayColumnKey => 'title';

  @override
  List<BeakColumn> get columns => NoteColumns.values;

  @override
  List<Enum> get formSlots => _NoteModelFormSlot.values;
}
```

| Override | Emitted when |
| --- | --- |
| `table`, `displayColumnKey`, `columns`, `formSlots` | always |
| `validationRules`, `behavior`, `permissions`, `capabilities` | the schema class declares the matching `static` getter, see [Annotations](annotations.md#beakschema) |
| `relatedModels` | the schema has a relationship |
| `relationships` | the schema has a relationship or an inverse |
| `softDeletes => true` | `@Resource(softDeletes: true)` |

`options` and `search` return a `BeakOptionQuery` for a picker. `search` covers the display column and every `searchable` column that is not a password.

### XDraft, XRecord and the access extensions

`XDraft` reads a live form draft through a `BeakDraftReader`, so a value is nullable until the form completes it. `XRecord` is an extension type over `BeakRecord`, a zero-cost view whose getters return the declared Dart type. A required column reads with `require` and throws a `BeakRecordShapeException` naming the column if the record lacks it. A relationship getter returns the eager-loaded rows as `List<YRecord>` (empty when not loaded) or `YRecord?` for a to-one.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.beak.dart"
extension type const NoteRecord._(BeakRecord record) {
  /// Views [record] as a notes row.
  const NoteRecord.of(BeakRecord record) : this._(record);

  /// Primary key.
  String? get id => NoteColumns.id.readFrom(record);
```

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/resources/notes/models/note.beak.dart"
extension NoteRecordAccess on BeakRecord {
  /// This record, typed as a notes row.
  NoteRecord get asNote => NoteRecord.of(this);
}
```

### Reserved names

A field named like a member of `BeakModel` gets no static shortcut on `XModel`, and a field named like a member of the path API gets none on `XToOneField`. Reach it through `XModel.fields.<name>` and `XToOneField.fields.<name>`.

| Class | Names with no shortcut |
| --- | --- |
| `XModel` | `fields`, `options`, `search`, `table`, `displayColumnKey`, `columns`, `permissions`, `validationRules`, `behavior`, `capabilities`, `dataSource`, `createModel`, `editModel`, `relationships`, `relatedModels`, `softDeletes`, `formSlots`, `primaryKey`, `ref`, `query`, `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `sumDecimal`, `avgDecimal`, `summary`, `record`, `primaryKeyOf`, `columnsFor`, `columnByKey`, `relationshipByKey`, `toString`, `noSuchMethod`, `hashCode`, `runtimeType` |
| `XToOneField` | `fields`, `model`, `path`, `isRequired`, `key`, `label`, `qualifiedKey`, `readFrom`, `ownerRecord`, `relation`, `target`, `relationLoad`, `linkTo`, `invalid`, `eq`, `equalsId`, `matches`, `options`, `hashCode`, `runtimeType`, `toString`, `noSuchMethod` |

A field named `record` is the one name with no fallback: the typed record view wraps the underlying record as `record`, so `beak prepare` refuses it with `cannot be generated`. Rename the field and keep the stored name with `@Column(columnName:)`. A schema class cannot itself be named `List`, `String`, `Future`, `Function`, `Enum`, `DateTime`, `Schema`, `Migration`, `BeakSchema`, `Resource`, `Column`, `Display` or one of the relationship annotations, because the generated code uses those names.

## Wiring files

The registry lists every model and builds the `BeakModelRegistry`:

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/beak/registry.g.dart"
/// Every model discovered under `lib/`, in path order.
const List<BeakModel> beakModels = <BeakModel>[NoteModel()];

/// A registry populated with every model in [beakModels].
BeakModelRegistry buildBeakRegistry() {
  final registry = BeakModelRegistry();
  for (final model in beakModels) {
    registry.register(model);
  }
  return registry;
}
```

The panel config has one `BeakResource` per shown model, presented as `beak.yaml` says. A `BeakResource` class you wrote replaces the default of the model it configures, and a class whose model is hidden or unknown is still added.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/beak/panel.g.dart"
BeakPanelConfig buildBeakPanel() {
  final config = BeakPanelConfig(
    title: 'Quickstart',
    apiBaseUrl: const String.fromEnvironment(
      'BEAK_API_BASE_URL',
      defaultValue: 'http://localhost:8080',
    ),
    sidebarCollapsible: true,
    sidebarDefaultCollapsed: false,
    resources: [
      BeakResource(
        model: const NoteModel(),
        icon: BeakIconToken(OiIcons.fileText),
        navigationGroup: 'Content',
      ),
    ],
  );
  return config;
}
```

`app.g.dart` builds that config once at startup (it holds closures and block trees, so a fresh one per frame would rebuild the router) and wraps it:

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/beak/app.g.dart"
final BeakPanelConfig beakPanelConfig = buildBeakPanel();

/// The Quickstart panel.
final class BeakApp extends StatelessWidget {
  /// Creates the app; [dataSource] injects a fake in widget tests.
  const BeakApp({this.dataSource, super.key});

  /// Test seam replacing the HTTP-backed data source.
  final BeakDataSource? dataSource;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) =>
      BeakPanel(config: beakPanelConfig, dataSource: dataSource);
}
```

`server.g.dart` builds the backend host. It registers the two framework migrations first, then yours in the order of their declared `name`, which is why a generated migration's name starts with a timestamp.

```dart title="examples/quickstart/lib/beak/server.g.dart"
BeakServeHost beakHost({Map<String, String>? environment}) => BeakServeHost(
  environment: environment,
  registry: buildBeakRegistry(),
  migrations: const [
    BeakCommitReceiptsMigration(),
    BeakOutboxMigration(),
    CreateNotesTable(),
  ],
  seeders: const [],
);
```

A `server:` block in `beak.yaml` is a default for `environment`: a real `PORT` in the process still decides where it binds.

## Migrations

Migrations are the one generated thing you own afterwards. `beak prepare` writes a migration for each table that has none, once, and never rewrites it.

```dart
// Migrations before the wiring: a migration Beak writes must be visible to
// the scan that lists them on the generated host. They are written once and
// never rewritten, so they deliberately sit outside BeakEmitters.all, whose
// every entry `beak doctor` byte-compares and would call stale.
final migrationFiles = <String>[];
for (final migration in BeakMigrationEmitter.missing(
  models: discovery.models,
  schemas: schemas,
  coveredTables: discovery.migratedTables,
  now: environment.now(),
)) {
  final file = File('${root.path}/${migration.path}');
  if (file.existsSync()) {
    continue;
  }
  file.parent.createSync(recursive: true);
  file.writeAsStringSync(migration.contents);
  migrationFiles.add(migration.path);
}
```

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Path | `lib/migrations/create_<table>_table.dart`, and `create_<a>_<b>_table.dart` for a pivot |
| Class and name | `Create<Table>Table`, with a `name` of `<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>_create_<table>_table` |
| Order | Dependency order, a belongs-to target before its referrer. Each file's timestamp is one second after the previous. The generated host registers the migrations in that order even when a table gained its key later, see [Migrations](../backend/migrations.md#order) |
| Body | Reads the model through `BeakBlueprint` when it runs, so a database that has not run it yet gets the table the model describes today. A database that has run it needs `beak make:migration <Name> --from-drift` for a column added later |
| Skipped | A schema with `@Resource(managesSchema: false)`, and any table that an existing migration in `lib/migrations/` already creates |
| Never | Auto-applied. `beak migrate` applies them, after you review them. |

## Rules and limits

- The part file and the wiring files are overwritten without asking. Keep hand-written code in other files.
- A schema class needs `part '<file>.beak.dart';` naming its own part, and the generated file names the library with `part of`. `beak prepare` and `beak doctor` refuse a schema file without the directive.
- `*.beak.dart` files are committed and `beak prepare` output is deterministic, so a diff after `beak prepare` means a schema, a resource or `beak.yaml` changed.
- `beak dev` runs `beak prepare` before serving. A schema error stops it with the list above.
- Field slots (`_XModelFormSlot`) are an implementation bridge: the auto forms key fields by an enum, so each model gets one value per column and relationship. The names `s0`, `s1` are meaningless on purpose.
- The default table name uses a small pluraliser, see [Annotations](annotations.md#rules-and-limits).

## Source

- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/schema/beak_schema_emitter.dart` writes the schema part.
- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/schema/beak_schema_reader.dart` reads the schema classes into the emitter's model.
- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/project/beak_emitters.dart` writes the registry, panel, app, server and entrypoint files.
- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/project/beak_discovery.dart` finds models, resources, screens, migrations, seeders and overrides.
- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/schema/beak_migration_emitter.dart` writes the missing migrations.
- `packages/beak_cli/lib/src/commands/prepare_command.dart` runs the whole pass.
- `examples/quickstart/lib/beak` holds real output of the wiring files.
